marker.description: Green-headed pin indicating a structure in the diencephalon/thalamus region.

main_question: Identify the structure indicated by the green pin.
main_explanation: The pin is located in the large ovoid mass of grey matter situated in the diencephalon, superior to the midbrain and posterior to the lateral ventricle, which corresponds to the thalamus.

supporting_question.question: Which of the following is a primary function of the structure indicated by the pin?
options: Regulation of body temperature and hunger
Relay of sensory and motor signals to the cerebral cortex
Coordination of voluntary movement and balance
supporting_question.explanation: The thalamus acts as a major relay station for sensory and motor signals to the cerebral cortex, as well as for the regulation of consciousness, sleep, and alertness.
